question: Which compiler contract retains repeated ordinary shared vector loads, and what does it leave unguaranteed?

findings.fact: C++ asm volatile prevents assembly deletion or movement during PTX generation. A memory clobber constrains front-end memory optimization around hidden memory side effects. Neither statement promises preservation of a nonvolatile PTX load through later assembly optimization.
findings.implication: The observed ptxas hoisting is not contradicted by the documented front-end contract.

findings.fact: The volatile load syntax permits shared space and v2/v4.b32 vectors; cache modifiers are disallowed.
findings.implication: Use ld.volatile.shared.v2.b32 or ld.volatile.shared.v4.b32 for the repeated-load control.

findings.fact: Volatile instruction count is preserved. Volatile instructions retain order relative to each other, but their memory operations may reorder or merge.
findings.implication: Confirm native load width and dynamic request counts. Volatile is not a guarantee of a separate physical transaction for every instruction or a general fence.

findings.fact: Each address must align to the complete access size: 8 bytes for v2.b32 and 16 for v4.b32; misalignment is undefined.
findings.implication: Retain the aligned per-lane word offsets in the prepared sweep.

experiment_acceptance.functional: Check numerical values independently of dynamic instruction retention. Correct values alone can survive a hoisted constant load.
experiment_acceptance.compiled: Require the intended native 64/128-bit LDS instruction inside the repeated loop after ptxas.
experiment_acceptance.dynamic: Use repeated-iteration minus zero-iteration counters to confirm repeated requests and service work.
experiment_acceptance.timing: Use the volatile variant to identify splitting only. Do not transfer its timing to ordinary GEMM loads without an additional equivalence check.

current_wide_broadcast_observation.origin: Parent message, preliminary hardware observation; not independently verified by this literature worker
current_wide_broadcast_observation.value: One native 128-bit same-vector read reportedly generated two wavefronts.
current_wide_broadcast_observation.interpretation: Potentially rejects one whole-warp merged service package, but repeated-load confirmation and exact native instruction must precede admission.
current_wide_broadcast_observation.missing: Fixed lane groups, masked-lane handling, arbitration and physical bank ports remain unidentified.

candidate_field_impacts.F052: Improves the benchmark contract; no additional full identification.
candidate_field_impacts.F053: Wide broadcast observation requires hardware confirmation; ordinary same-word broadcast does not settle it.
